1.
List has been revised.
2. Supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Ajay Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rajendra Prasad Maury,
learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Arun Kumar Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
4.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.174 of 2024, under Sections 354, 376, 364, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C., Police Station- Manikpur, District- Chitrakoot, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, the applicant alongwith co-accused persons is stated to have committed gang-rape with the victim on 15.8.2023 at about 07:00 a.m.
The victim is stated to have been retrieved by the police the same day and entered the matter in record books.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The FIR is delayed by more than one year and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
The victim has misused the process of court.

Although the victim, whose statement has been recorded during trial, has categorically stated that applicant has raped her, but the said story stands falsified from the fact that she has stated that she had gone to study in school on the alleged date while it was a public holiday and only flag is hoisted on that date.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that the father of the victim owed an amount of Rs.80,000/- towards the applicant and the said fact that a Panchayat was held in front of house of the victim regarding payment of said money has been admitted by the victim in her cross-examination, as such, it is a clear cut case of false implication.
There is no criminal antecedent of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 10.11.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
8. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the bail application.

9. In light of the judgement of the Supreme Court passed in Niranjan Singh and another vs Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785, this Court has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.text: Niranjan Singh and another vs Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.

10. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant- Lal Singh Alias Kaira, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S.

13. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
